what: Laureate Education runs private universities in Mexico and Peru. After selling its operations in other countries, it now focuses on two markets, with brands such as Universidad del Valle de México and UNITEC in Mexico, and Universidad Peruana de Ciencias Aplicadas, Universidad Privada del Norte and Cibertec in Peru. It offers campus-based and online degrees.
customers: Students in Mexico and Peru, mostly working adults and young people from middle-income families, paying tuition themselves or with family support.
money: UPC, UPN and Cibertec universities and institutes.
UVM and UNITEC universities with campus and online programmes.
moat: Laureate’s universities have strong brands, accreditation and campus networks built over decades, which are difficult for new entrants to copy. Demand for higher education in both countries is growing faster than public university capacity, and Laureate’s scale lets it run campuses efficiently and invest in online and hybrid programmes.
risks: Results are reported in dollars but earned in Mexican pesos and Peruvian soles, so currency moves swing reported numbers.
Political and regulatory risk in Mexico and Peru, including changes to education rules and taxes.
The company depends on just two countries.
Trailing net income includes items that are unlikely to repeat; forward earnings put the shares on about 18 times.
Economic downturns can reduce enrolment among price-sensitive students.
opportunities: Revenue grew from $1.09B in 2021 to $1.92B over the last twelve months.
Free cash flow of $288M is about 6.4% of the market value.
Buybacks cut the share count from 190M to 149M since 2021.
EV/EBITDA of about 9 is undemanding for a business growing enrolment steadily.
watch: Enrolment growth in Mexico and Peru, currency moves, tuition increases and buybacks.
view: Laureate has become a simple story after years of complexity: two countries, growing enrolment and cash that goes back to shareholders. After selling its other universities, the company has focused on Mexico and Peru, where demand for private higher education is strong and Laureate’s brands are among the best known. Revenue rose from $1.09B in 2021 to $1.92B over the last twelve months.

The earnings picture needs care. Trailing net income of $388M includes favourable items, which is why the trailing P/E of 12 drops into an 18 times forward multiple. A better anchor is EV/EBITDA near 9 and a free cash flow yield of about 6%, both reasonable for a business with steady volume growth and pricing power. Share buybacks have shrunk the share count by more than a fifth since 2021.

The investment turns on emerging-market risk rather than the business. If the peso and sol hold and both governments leave private education alone, Laureate should compound at high single digits plus buybacks. I think it is fairly priced to slightly cheap; the currency and political exposure is the reason it trades at a discount, and investors must be comfortable with that.
bull: Enrolment keeps growing in both countries, currencies stay stable and buybacks drive double-digit per-share growth.
bear: A currency slide or regulatory change in Mexico or Peru cuts dollar earnings sharply.
